title: Does anyone use ChatGPT / Codex for Unity game development?
author: BlackenedSpektrum
selftext:
I bought a one-month Claude subscription to see what it was capable of. I built a small game prototype with gameplay mechanics, animations, combat, design, and so on. Claude handled everything surprisingly well, and I was genuinely impressed.

It wrote code, and not once did I run into any major hallucinations or serious mistakes. Everything went pretty smoothly. It also helped me a lot with optimizing 3D models — reducing their polygon counts directly through Blender scripts, creating new tools for Unity that I could use to streamline my development workflow, and so on.

However, since I'm from an unsupported country, when I renewed my subscription after a month, I was asked to complete verification. I went through it, but then they requested KYC verification again. Long story short, I don't see a way to keep using Claude anymore.

So here's my question: has anyone switched to Codex after using Claude? Is it just as good at game development, from writing code to helping with 3D modeling workflows?

I'm just not sure whether I should give ChatGPT a try or just say fuck it and give up on game development altogether?

comments.author: i_edit_text
comments.body: Its really good, I use both. I'd describe claude as powerful, fast, expensive and gpt as powerful, slow and cheap.

comments.author: Successful_Dream_929
comments.body:
well depends on what model you were using on claude and what model you will use on the codex app.
You can throw anything on Opus 5.5 and it just does it. But not true for for example sonnet. I assume you arent doing anything special cus you wouldnt ask this question otherwise so if you switch to codex, you can throw anything at Sol and i think it can handle it. Also you get chatgpt pro too with the nearly unlimited image generation tho so thats a plus.
But since you tried out opus with a full game basically, do the same task on codex Sol i think and see for yourself. I used both, most of the mistakes their made was because of me being lazy not designing my systems enough or using lazy prompts.

comments.author: daddy_reloaded
comments.body:
I have both Claude and codex at the highest plan. 
Codex tends to be slowest, and I tend to use Claude for coding task more than codex, but just by habit, but every PR is reviewed by codex and every time it found something to correct. So complementary. 
In the other hand, codex is really mandatory for Image and textures generation drafting. And currently I found astra more powerful than fable for drafting 3d meshes. 
So I think there is no real winner.
